Subject: Deployment mode & cost model — post-call recap and next steps

Thanks again for the call this morning — great to meet the Finlytics team. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned:

Key requirements we heard:
- Strong data residency requirement (US-only) and need for audit logs (SOC 2)
- Expected steady-state volume: ~120M tokens/day (burst to 250M/day)
- Latency target: 95th <= 300ms for single-request text generation (chat flows)
- Timeline: pilot in 6–8 weeks, production roll in Q3

Deployment modes we discussed:
- Hosted API: fastest to ship, pay-as-you-go per-token; good for initial pilot but higher per-token cost at scale
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): dedicated GPU pools, predictable throughput, reserved commits reduce unit cost; recommended if you need consistent low latency and cost predictability
- Private (VPC / on-prem): for strict security/regulatory setups — higher up-front fees, on-prem licensing or private control plane

Action items / asks for Finlytics:
1) Can you confirm the 120M tokens/day steady-state and typical request size (avg tokens per request)?
2) Any hard constraints on latency (beyond 95th <= 300ms) or max cold-start tolerances?
3) Who should we loop in on procurement/legal for SOW / security questionnaire?

I've attached a draft pricing summary (high-level) that maps the three modes to ballpark economics and reserved commit options. Aditya (cc) will pull a more detailed cost model once we get the confirmed numbers above.

Next step proposal:
- You share avg tokens/request and procurement contact by Mon Mar 22
- We deliver a 2-sheet cost model and recommended deployment mode by Fri Mar 26
- Optional: 45-minute technical deep-dive with our infra lead the week of Mar 29 if you want bench/latency proofs

Attachments: redwood_pricing_draft.pdf (PDF, 320KB); SOW-draft.docx (DOCX, 24KB)

Thanks — look forward to the next steps.

Best,
Marissa

Following up with a preliminary cost sketch based on the numbers Sofia provided. These are high-level and intended to help Finlytics compare economics quickly — I can produce a spreadsheet with line-item assumptions when we lock avg tokens/request and burst profile.

Assumptions used:
- Steady: 120M tokens/day (3.6B tokens/month)
- Burst: up to 250M tokens/day for short windows
- Model: mid-tier open LLM (quantized), inference cost baseline used for per-token hosted estimate

1) Hosted API (pay-as-you-go)
- Nominal per-token: $0.0025 per 1K tokens (example) => ~$9,000 per day @120M tokens (~$270K/mo)
- Pros: no commit, simplest to start
- Cons: highest unit cost at scale, potential latency variance during noisy neighbors (we can provide region pinning)

2) Dedicated (reserved capacity) — 12m vs 36m commit examples
- With a 12-month reserved commit we can offer ~35–45% effective reduction vs hosted per-token (depends on chosen GPU tier & batching)
- With 36-month commit we can offer ~50–65% reduction (larger discount for longer commitments + reserved instance utilization)
- Ballpark: effective $/1M tokens could drop to $800–1,200 per 1M (vs hosted ~$2,500 per 1M) depending on config and batching
- Pros: predictable monthly costs, lower per-token unit economics, dedicated latency SLOs
- Cons: commit required; needs capacity planning and forecast alignment

3) Private (VPC / on-prem)
- One-time onboarding & integration: $75k–$150k (depends on on-prem vs VPC, KMS/HSM integration complexity)
- Monthly platform fee + support: $15k–$40k/mo depending on support tier and retention windows
- Effective per-token cost can be lowest if you fully utilize hardware, but higher upfront & operational responsibilities

Next steps I recommend:
- We model a 12- and 36-month reserved commit for the Dedicated option showing effective $/1M tokens and monthly Opex (I can run this once we confirm avg tokens/request and expected utilization).
- If Finlytics prefers a low-risk pilot, start on Hosted for 4–8 weeks to validate latency/quality and then flip to Dedicated with reserved commit for production. We can also set up a Private evaluation if compliance requires it.

I'll prepare a spreadsheet and a 2-slide summary by Mar 26 per Marissa's timeline.
